name: Cleveland Cavaliers
desc: NBA basketball franchise based in Cleveland, Ohio, majority-owned by Dan Gilbert since 2005.
ownership: majority-owned by Dan Gilbert; minority stake held by Blue Owl's HomeCourt Partners fund (since Jul 2026)
capacity_detail: Valued at USD 4.86B by Sportico (cited by Bloomberg Government, Jul 2026); Forbes' January 2026 ranking put it at USD 4.8B with revenue of USD 440M
markets: United States; plays in the NBA from Cleveland, Ohio, with roots and fan base in Ohio

signals.raise: Blue Owl HomeCourt Partners fund bought a minority equity stake, terms not disclosed (Jul 2026; https://www.blueowl.com/news/blue-owls-homecourt-partners-fund-announces-minority-equity-investment-cleveland-cavaliers)

rationale: Sports property rather than sponsor; possible cross-promotion or hospitality tie-ins with F1, but low fit as a paying F1 partner.

name: Rawlings Sporting Goods
desc: Maker of baseball and softball gloves, bats, balls and protective gear; official ball supplier to Major League Baseball.
ownership: subsidiary of Partners Group (majority, agreed Nov 2026); existing shareholders incl. Seidler Equity Partners and MLB keep meaningful ownership
capacity_detail: Partners Group agreed to buy a majority at an enterprise value of around USD 2B, per a person familiar (Bloomberg via Swissinfo, 19 Nov 2026); terms not disclosed by the buyer
sponsorships: Official supplier of Major League Baseball balls (since 1977; single MLB ball since 2000); sponsors over 50 NCAA Division 1 baseball teams
markets: United States baseball and softball market, with brands Rawlings, Easton, Combat, Miken, Worth and D-BAT training academies

signals.raise: Partners Group agreed to buy a majority stake at an EV of around USD 2B (Nov 2026; https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/partners-group-snaps-up-majority-in-rawlings-sporting-goods/92408562)

rationale: Heritage sports-equipment brand under new owner; F1 exposure is a weak fit for a US baseball-focused product range.
